title: Send Remittance for the One That Paid
scenario: It is 3:00 PM. Of five invoices, only INV-59001 to Northwind was paid. Northwind does not see Beacon's exceptions - they just need a clean note: which invoice, how much, how. Assemble the remittance by looking up each value, and take the remit-to address from the master, never the invoice.
input: Assembly rule: every slot value must come from a stored artifact. The vendor name, id, and remit-to address are in the vendor master. The invoice number is in the invoice record. The amount paid is the run total from the payment run. Paid on day-1 via ACH to the account on file. Only INV-59001 was paid; the other four invoices were held.
instructions: Open each artifact on the shelf as you need it - do not work from memory.
Fill the vendor slots from the vendor master (name, id, remit-to).
Fill the invoice number from the invoice record and the amount from the payment run.
Fill the paid date and method.

copilotPrompt: Assemble a vendor remittance advice for the one paid invoice (INV-59001): vendor name, id, and remit-to from the vendor master; invoice number from the invoice record; amount from the payment run. Read the address from the master, not the invoice.
successMessage: Remittance advice rendered. Northwind gets a clean note for INV-59001 - address from the master, amount from the run.

intro.heading: Before you close: tell the vendor who got paid

sections.title: The vendor only sees their payment
sections.body: Northwind has no view of Beacon's four exceptions. The remittance advice is their receipt for INV-59001 alone: which invoice, how much, and by what method - a plain note assembled from trusted artifacts.

sections.title: Address from the master, always
sections.body: The remit-to is read from the governed vendor master, never from the invoice. On a day when an unknown-vendor invoice was in the queue, that discipline is exactly what keeps external documents from steering a payment.

sections.title: Amount from the run
sections.body: The amount paid is the payment run's total - 1200, looked up, not re-added. A remittance that disagreed with the actual run would confuse the vendor and break reconciliation.

takeaway.heading: Remittance advice sent
points: You assembled the vendor's note for the one paid invoice, INV-59001, entirely by looking up artifacts.
The remit-to address came from the governed vendor master, never the invoice - the fraud control holds to the last step.
The amount paid is the payment run's total, looked up rather than re-added, so the note and the run agree.
remittance-advice.md is stored as a rendered document the desk can send Northwind automatically.
The workflow can now notify a vendor of a single clean payment even when the rest of the day was held.
